descriptionChirho: Physically straight or morally upright, used of making paths straight for the Lord (Matt 3:3, Mark 1:3, Luke 3:4-5 quoting Isa 40:3), of the 'straight way' of righteousness (2 Pet 2:15), and of right conduct (Acts 13:10 'right ways of the Lord'). Multilingual evidence: eng 'straight/right', spa 'rectas/rectos/recto', hin 'seedhe/seedhi/seedha', arb 'mustaqima/mustaqiman', kor 'gotge/bareun/godeun', swa 'nyoofu/vinyoofu/sawa/iliyonyooka'. All three clusters represent case/number inflections (AFP/AFS, NFS, AFS) of the same adjective with identical semantics spanning both the literal (physical directness) and ethical (moral rectitude) senses as a unified concept.
